title: Post-acute viral infectious syndromes in Berlin (PAIS Berlin): Structured cross-sectoral and interdisciplinary care
summary:
PAIS Berlin focuses on the paitent journeys of adult patients with PAIS (persistent symptoms following a viral infection such as COVID-19) in Berlin who request for an appointment at one of the seven university outpatient clinics of the Charité.

The aim is to understand how these patients are treated and cared for within the healthcare system, which healthcare pathways they follow,  how current healthcare works for them and how different medical specialties are involved in their care. Based on this, a new model of care will be developed to inform future care privision and make it more sustainable and better tailored to the needs of the patients. PAIS Berlin study adresses five main areas:

1. Understanding how patients with varying severity and different symptoms are cared for and how they utilize the healthcare system.
2. Identifying where health care provision can be optimized or to detect system barriers -and improve patient cetered care.
3. Developing clear recommendations for diagnosis and treatment to ensure patients receive appropriate, effective care including collaboration across specialties.
4. Contributing to the tailoring of health service provision to better meet the diverse needs of patient groups.
5. Improving the organization of outpatient (non-hospital) care—especially for complex cases—to ensure it is effective, well-coordinated, and resource-efficient.

interventions.name: Patients with post-acute viral infectious syndromes in Berlin who request for a healthcare appointment at an outpatient clinic in Charité and receive healthcare appointment will be observed for 18 months.

Patients with post-acute viral infectious syndromes in Berlin who request for a healthcare appointment in an outpatient clinic in Charité and do not receive a healthcare appointment will be observed for 18 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Appointment request at one of the participating outpatient clinics of Charité due to symptoms limiting daily life, persisting for more than 3 months, and not explained by other diagnoses
2. Sufficient German language skills to participate in a questionnaire-based study
3. Statutory health insurance coverage (GKV-insured)
4. Residence in the Berlin metropolitan region
Exclusion criteria:
1. Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
2. Previous consultation at a PCN outpatient clinic or treatment within the last six months
3. Residence outside the Berlin metropolitan region
4. Privately insured or self-paying patients
